summary: Amin Sweeney worked in linguistics and related fields after completing his doctorate at the University of London (c. 1967–1970). He taught at the National University of Malaysia (1970–1977) and UC Berkeley (department chairman 1986–1991, emeritus in 1998).

Amita Chatterjee is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who taught Kuntala Bhattacharya. She served as a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University, where her posts are attested in 1999 and 2009.
Amod Jayant Lele is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Parimal G. Patil.

Amrit Madhav Ghatage was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor and Head of Linguistics at Deccan College (c. 1961–1978) and later as Vice-President of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (c. 1993–2003).
Amrith Krishna works in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held a post at the University of Cambridge, as well as positions attested at Uniphore in 2023 and Learno.AI in 2024–2025.

Amy Heller is a Tibetologist and historian who earned her PhD at EPHE under Ariane Macdonald. She held posts at CNRS, Yale (1982), Sichuan University (2007), Sapienza (2006–2008), SOAS (2011–2013), INALCO (2014–2016), and Bern (2017–2018).

Amy Paris Langenberg specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She completed her PhD at Columbia University (c. 2002–2008) and served as assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College (c. 2014–2020).

Amy Sims Miller works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her BA at Wesleyan and an MA and PhD at the University of Virginia (the latter under David Germano), while also training under several traditional teachers.
Amy Snyder Ohta is a scholar of linguistics and Japanology. She studied at UCLA (1990, 1993) and became a professor at the University of Washington (post c. 1995).

Anagarika Dharmapala was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at institutions including S. Thomas' College and Royal College, Colombo. He founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891 and the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

Anagarika Govinda studied across Europe, earning a doctorate at Freiburg and training under teachers including Tomo Geshe Rinpoche. He founded the Arya Maitreya Mandala in 1933 and taught at Visva-Bharati, Patna, Allahabad, Lucknow, and Banaras Hindu University.

Anagarika Munindra was a Buddhist studies figure who served as superintendent of the Mahabodhi Temple (1953–1957). He studied under Mahasi Sayadaw (1957–1966) and Satya Narayan Goenka, and taught Joseph Goldstein and Dipa Ma.
Anam Thubten Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar and teacher. He studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche and has served as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation.

Anand A. Yang is a historian and Indologist who studied at Swarthmore College and the University of Virginia. He held appointments at Sweet Briar College and the University of Utah before becoming a professor at the University of Washington (c. 2002).

Anand Venkatkrishnan works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at Columbia University (completed 2015) and holds an assistant professorship in the History of Religion in South Asia at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

Ananda Guruge studied at the University of Ceylon and the University of London. He held posts at the National Institute of Educational Planning and Administration (attested 1970), CSU Fullerton, and the University of the West (attested 2012).

Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy studied at University College London and under Caroline Rhys Davids. In Indology, philosophy, and art history, he directed Ceylon's Geological Survey (c. 1903–1906) and held curator and research posts at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1917, 1933).

Anant Sadashiv Altekar was an Indologist and historian. He was a department head at Banaras Hindu University (c. 1930–1949), chairman of the Numismatic Society of India (1947), professor at Patna University (c. 1949–1957), and director of K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1955).

Anantalal Thakur was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a professor at the Mithila Research Institute (c. 1957–1974) and as director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).

Anantanand Rambachan is an Indology, philosophy, and religion scholar educated at the University of the West Indies, under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, and at the University of Leeds. He served as professor of religion at St. Olaf College (c. 1985–2021).
